transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for making time to discuss the eighth-grade civics oral-history project. Before I can sign off on this, I'd like to walk through the draft plan together and make sure we've addressed any concerns. I understand the proposal involves 20 student interviewers, audio recording on personal phones, publication of all recordings on the public school website, and indefinite retention of the files. I'd like to hear everyone's thoughts on whether this plan is ready to move forward or if there are adjustments we should consider before approval.

transcript.text: I need to flag an important constraint before we go further. My project roster review shows that exactly eight students have completed the district's media-ethics training: J1, J3, J6, J8, J11, J14, J17, and J20. Only those eight may conduct recorded interviews, and the approval file must include a training-verification record. So the plan as drafted, with 20 student interviewers, cannot move forward without adjustment.

transcript.text: I've completed my family-consent review, and there's a significant issue we need to address. Five interviewees — I2, I5, I9, I14, and I18 — have not granted permission for public web publication. Their recordings may only be used in the school's internal archive, not on the public website. The plan must include a consent-exclusion record documenting this, and we cannot publish all 20 recordings publicly as the draft currently calls for.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I've completed my technology review, and there are several critical issues with the current plan. First, personal phones cannot be used for school recordings — the project must use district tablets instead. Second, the recordings must be stored in the restricted OralHistory drive, not published on the public school website. Third, the files must be deleted exactly 45 days after the final class presentation — indefinite retention is not permitted. Finally, the technology plan must include a secure-storage configuration record documenting these measures.
